272	//
273	// Trivy writes "AVD-DS-0002" in AVDID and "DS002" in ID, and which of the two
274	// reaches a Finding has changed before. Matching on either spelling costs one
275	// function; matching on one of them costs a catalog that silently stops firing
276	// the day the other is used.
277	func RuleKey(id string) string {
278		id = strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(id))
279		id = strings.TrimPrefix(id, "AVD-")
280		id = strings.ReplaceAll(id, "-", "")
281	
282		letters := strings.IndexFunc(id, func(r rune) bool { return r >= '0' && r <= '9' })
283		if letters <= 0 {
284			return id
285		}
286		prefix, digits := id[:letters], strings.TrimLeft(id[letters:], "0")
287		if digits == "" {
288			digits = "0"
289		}
290		return prefix + digits
291	}

293	// fixRootUser satisfies "specify at least 1 USER command" by creating an
294	// unprivileged account in the final stage and switching to it.
295	//
296	// **It creates the account rather than naming a uid.** A bare `USER 10001`
297	// switches to a uid that has no passwd entry: no name, no home, no shell. Much
298	// of what runs in a container asks the system who it is — anything calling
299	// getpwuid, a shell wanting $HOME, tools that write to a home directory — and
300	// all of it degrades in ways that surface later, at run time, far from this
301	// edit. `adduser` first, `USER appuser` after, is what `docker init` generates
302	// and what this now emits.
303	//
304	// **The flags are Debian's, so the base image has to be one.** The long options
305	// below belong to the Debian/Ubuntu `adduser`; busybox's, on Alpine, takes
306	// different ones (`-D`, `-H`, `-s /sbin/nologin`) and a distroless image has no
307	// shell to run either in. Guessing wrong produces a Dockerfile that fails at
308	// build, which is worse than offering nothing — so a base this cannot identify
309	// is declined, and the agent path (phase A) takes it.
310	//
311	// The block goes before the final stage's first CMD or ENTRYPOINT, which is
312	// where it has to be to apply to the process that runs — after it, it would
313	// change nothing. With neither, it goes at the end of the file.
314	//
315	// What it does not do is chown anything. A process that loses root may no longer
316	// be able to write where it used to, and no edit computed from the Dockerfile
317	// alone can know. That is a change the user reads in the diff and agrees to, and
318	// that the re-scan then confirms cleared the rule — it is not a claim that the
319	// image still works.
320	func fixRootUser(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
321		if !dockerfile.IsDockerfileName(baseName(f.File)) {
322			return nil, ReasonNotADockerfile
323		}
324		stages := dockerfile.Parse(content).Stages
325		if len(stages) == 0 {
326			return nil, ReasonNoStage
327		}
328	
329		final := stages[len(stages)-1]
330		if !isDebianFamily(final.Image) {
331			return nil, ReasonUnknownBaseFamily
332		}
333	
334		lines := contentLines(content)
335		if final.Line > len(lines) {
336			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
337		}
338	
339		at, already := insertionPoint(lines, final.Line, len(content))
340		if already {
341			return nil, ReasonAlreadyFixed
342		}
343	
344		text := addUserBlock(lineEnding(content))
345		if at == len(content) && !endsWithNewline(content) {
346			text = lineEnding(content) + text
347		}
348		return []patch.Edit{{Span: patch.Span{Start: at, End: at}, New: text}}, ""
349	}

351	// addUserBlock is the Debian/Ubuntu incantation, spelled out rather than
352	// condensed: every flag is there to make the account unusable for anything but
353	// running the process — no password, no home, no login shell.
354	func addUserBlock(eol string) string {
355		lines := []string{
356			"ARG UID=" + nonRootUID,
357			"RUN adduser \\",
358			`    --disabled-password \`,
359			`    --gecos "" \`,
360			`    --home "/nonexistent" \`,
361			`    --shell "/usr/sbin/nologin" \`,
362			"    --no-create-home \\",
363			`    --uid "${UID}" \`,
364			"    " + nonRootUser,
365			"USER " + nonRootUser,
366		}
367		return strings.Join(lines, eol) + eol
368	}

370	// recommendsFlag is what fixAptGetNoRecommends adds. Its position relative to
371	// "install" does not matter to apt-get, so the fix always puts it in the same
372	// place — right after "install" — rather than trying to match wherever a
373	// human might have put the rest of the command's own flags.
374	const recommendsFlag = "--no-install-recommends"
375	
376	// aptGetInstall matches an apt-get install invocation. It does not try to
377	// mirror the full breadth of Trivy's own check (flags between "apt-get" and
378	// "install" are rare enough to skip), because a match here only has to find
379	// what to fix, not decide what Trivy would flag — that decision was already
380	// made when the finding was reported.
381	var aptGetInstall = regexp.MustCompile(`apt-get\s+install\b`)
382	
383	// apkAdd matches an apk add invocation, on the same terms as aptGetInstall.
384	var apkAdd = regexp.MustCompile(`apk\s+add\b`)
385	
386	// assumeYesFlag recognizes apt-get's confirmation flag in any of the forms
387	// apt-get itself accepts: a short flag cluster containing 'y' (`-y`, `-qy`,
388	// `-yq`), or the long spellings. A literal `strings.Contains(s, "-y")` — good
389	// enough for the long, unique --no-install-recommends — would miss `-qy`.
390	var assumeYesFlag = regexp.MustCompile(`(^|\s)-[A-Za-z]*y[A-Za-z]*(\s|$)|--yes\b|--assume-yes\b`)
391	
392	// fixCommandFlag is fixAptGetNoRecommends, fixAptGetAssumeYes and
393	// fixApkNoCache's shared shape: find every invocation of the command the
394	// finding's line range covers, and add insertText right after it unless
395	// hasFlag already reports the flag present in that invocation's own
396	// statement.
397	//
398	// It only looks at the reported span, not the whole file: an invocation
399	// elsewhere in the Dockerfile is a different finding, and fixing it here
400	// would be an edit the diff never explained. Within the span, each invocation
401	// is checked on its own — a RUN chaining two of them with `&&` where only one
402	// already has the flag is not "already fixed" just because the flag appears
403	// somewhere in the line.
404	func fixCommandFlag(content []byte, f scan.Finding, command *regexp.Regexp, hasFlag func(string) bool, insertText, noMatchReason string) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
405		if !dockerfile.IsDockerfileName(baseName(f.File)) {
406			return nil, ReasonNotADockerfile
407		}
408		span, ok := lineSpan(content, f.Line, f.EndLine)
409		if !ok {
410			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
411		}
412		text := string(content[span.Start:span.End])
413	
414		matches := command.FindAllStringIndex(text, -1)
415		if matches == nil {
416			return nil, noMatchReason
417		}
418	
419		var edits []patch.Edit
420		for _, m := range matches {
421			stmtEnd := statementEnd(text, m[1])
422			if hasFlag(text[m[1]:stmtEnd]) {
423				continue
424			}
425			at := span.Start + m[1]
426			edits = append(edits, patch.Edit{Span: patch.Span{Start: at, End: at}, New: insertText})
427		}
428		if len(edits) == 0 {
429			return nil, ReasonAlreadyFixed
430		}
431		return edits, ""
432	}

434	// fixAptGetNoRecommends satisfies "'apt-get' missing '--no-install-recommends'"
435	// (AVD-DS-0029).
436	func fixAptGetNoRecommends(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
437		return fixCommandFlag(content, f, aptGetInstall,
438			func(s string) bool { return strings.Contains(s, recommendsFlag) },
439			" "+recommendsFlag, ReasonNoAptGetInstall)

454	// yumInstall, dnfInstall, microdnfInstall and zypperInstall match the install
455	// invocation fixAppendCleanup looks for, one per package manager.

457		yumInstall      = regexp.MustCompile(`yum\s+install\b`)
458		dnfInstall      = regexp.MustCompile(`dnf\s+install\b`)

463	// fixAppendCleanup is fixYumClean, fixDnfClean, fixMicrodnfClean and
464	// fixZypperClean's shared shape: Trivy's own check for each of these only
465	// counts a cleanup command as satisfying it when it is the last thing the RUN
466	// does, so the fix appends cleanCmd at the very end of the reported span
467	// rather than placing it next to the install call — anywhere else, a
468	// re-scan would still flag it.
469	//
470	// It is idempotent against the one case worth checking without a full shell
471	// parse: the span, once trailing whitespace and a stray continuation
472	// backslash are trimmed, already ending in cleanCmd.
473	func fixAppendCleanup(content []byte, f scan.Finding, install *regexp.Regexp, cleanCmd, noMatchReason string) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
474		if !dockerfile.IsDockerfileName(baseName(f.File)) {
475			return nil, ReasonNotADockerfile
476		}
477		span, ok := lineSpan(content, f.Line, f.EndLine)
478		if !ok {
479			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
480		}
481		text := string(content[span.Start:span.End])
482		if !install.MatchString(text) {
483			return nil, noMatchReason
484		}
485	
486		trimmed := strings.TrimRight(text, " \t\r\n")
487		trimmed = strings.TrimRight(strings.TrimSuffix(trimmed, "\\"), " \t")
488		if strings.HasSuffix(trimmed, cleanCmd) {
489			return nil, ReasonAlreadyFixed
490		}
491		at := span.Start + len(trimmed)
492		return []patch.Edit{{Span: patch.Span{Start: at, End: at}, New: " && " + cleanCmd}}, ""
493	}

516	// addUnsafe are the substrings that make an ADD instruction do something COPY
517	// cannot: extract a local tar archive, or fetch from a URL. Trivy's own check
518	// already excludes every ADD carrying one of these from AVD-DS-0005, so a
519	// finding reaching this fix is one it has already proven is a plain copy —
520	// this re-checks the live file rather than trusting a finding computed from a
521	// version of it that may have since changed.
522	var addUnsafe = []string{".tar", "http://", "https://", "git@"}
523	
524	// fixAddInsteadOfCopy satisfies "ADD instead of COPY" (AVD-DS-0005) by
525	// swapping the instruction's own keyword. Every argument is left untouched:
526	// COPY and ADD take the same syntax for a plain file copy, which is the only
527	// case this fix ever sees.
528	func fixAddInsteadOfCopy(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
529		if !dockerfile.IsDockerfileName(baseName(f.File)) {
530			return nil, ReasonNotADockerfile
531		}
532		lines := contentLines(content)
533		if f.Line < 1 || f.Line > len(lines) {
534			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
535		}
536		first := lines[f.Line-1]
537		if instruction(first.text) != "ADD" {
538			return nil, ReasonNotAnAddInstruction
539		}
540		span, ok := lineSpan(content, f.Line, f.EndLine)
541		if !ok {
542			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
543		}
544		text := string(content[span.Start:span.End])
545		for _, unsafe := range addUnsafe {
546			if strings.Contains(text, unsafe) {
547				return nil, ReasonAddExtractsOrFetches
548			}
549		}
550	
551		kw, ok := keywordSpan(first)
552		if !ok {
553			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
554		}
555		old := first.text[kw.Start-first.off : kw.End-first.off]
556		return []patch.Edit{{Span: kw, Old: old, New: "COPY"}}, ""
557	}

559	// fixCopyMissingTrailingSlash satisfies "COPY with more than two arguments
560	// not ending with slash" (AVD-DS-0011) by appending "/" to the destination —
561	// the last argument, since COPY only accepts a directory as its destination
562	// once it has more than one source.
563	func fixCopyMissingTrailingSlash(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
564		if !dockerfile.IsDockerfileName(baseName(f.File)) {
565			return nil, ReasonNotADockerfile
566		}
567		lines := contentLines(content)
568		if f.Line < 1 || f.Line > len(lines) {
569			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
570		}
571		if instruction(lines[f.Line-1].text) != "COPY" {
572			return nil, ReasonNotACopyInstruction
573		}
574		span, ok := lineSpan(content, f.Line, f.EndLine)
575		if !ok {
576			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
577		}
578		text := string(content[span.Start:span.End])
579	
580		fields := strings.Fields(stripContinuations(text))
581		var nonFlag []string
582		for _, a := range fields[1:] { // fields[0] is the COPY keyword itself
583			if !strings.HasPrefix(a, "--") {
584				nonFlag = append(nonFlag, a)
585			}
586		}
587		if len(nonFlag) <= 2 {
588			return nil, ReasonCopyHasTooFewArgs
589		}
590		if strings.HasSuffix(nonFlag[len(nonFlag)-1], "/") {
591			return nil, ReasonAlreadyFixed
592		}
593	
594		trimmed := strings.TrimRight(text, " \t\r\n")
595		at := span.Start + len(trimmed)
596		return []patch.Edit{{Span: patch.Span{Start: at, End: at}, New: "/"}}, ""
597	}

599	// fixMaintainerDeprecated satisfies "Deprecated MAINTAINER used"
600	// (AVD-DS-0022) by rewriting the whole instruction as the LABEL Docker itself
601	// has documented as the replacement since 1.13.0.
602	func fixMaintainerDeprecated(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
603		if !dockerfile.IsDockerfileName(baseName(f.File)) {
604			return nil, ReasonNotADockerfile
605		}
606		lines := contentLines(content)
607		if f.Line < 1 || f.Line > len(lines) {
608			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
609		}
610		l := lines[f.Line-1]
611		if instruction(l.text) != "MAINTAINER" {
612			return nil, ReasonNotAMaintainerInstruction
613		}
614		if strings.HasSuffix(strings.TrimRight(l.text, " \t"), "\\") {
615			return nil, ReasonMaintainerContinues
616		}
617	
618		sep := strings.IndexAny(l.text, " \t")
619		if sep < 0 {
620			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
621		}
622		value := strings.TrimSpace(l.text[sep+1:])
623		value = strings.Trim(value, `"'`)
624		value = strings.ReplaceAll(value, `"`, `\"`)
625	
626		old := l.text
627		return []patch.Edit{{
628			Span: patch.Span{Start: l.off, End: l.off + len(l.text)},
629			Old:  old,
630			New:  `LABEL maintainer="` + value + `"`,
631		}}, ""
632	}

634	// statementEnd finds where the shell statement starting at from ends: the next
635	// `&&` or `;`, or the end of text when neither separates it from what follows.
636	// A RUN chaining several commands is one Dockerfile instruction but several
637	// statements, and the flag has to be checked against the one that matched, not
638	// against whatever a later statement in the same RUN happens to contain.
639	func statementEnd(text string, from int) int {
640		end := len(text)
641		for _, sep := range []string{"&&", ";"} {
642			if i := strings.Index(text[from:], sep); i >= 0 && from+i < end {
643				end = from + i
644			}
645		}
646		return end
647	}
648	
649	// lineSpan returns the byte range covering lines startLine..endLine (1-based,
650	// inclusive) of content. endLine before startLine — including zero, which is
651	// what a finding cached before EndLine was recorded carries — is treated as a
652	// single-line span rather than declined outright: most apt-get installs are
653	// one physical line, and a finding that predates EndLine still names one.
654	func lineSpan(content []byte, startLine, endLine int) (patch.Span, bool) {
655		if endLine < startLine {
656			endLine = startLine
657		}
658		lines := contentLines(content)
659		if startLine < 1 || startLine > len(lines) || endLine > len(lines) {
660			return patch.Span{}, false
661		}
662		last := lines[endLine-1]
663		return patch.Span{Start: lines[startLine-1].off, End: last.off + len(last.text)}, true
664	}

666	// debianFamilyBases are the official images that build on Debian or Ubuntu
667	// unless their tag says otherwise.
668	//
669	// The list is short and conservative on purpose: an image missing from it is
670	// declined, which costs a fix, while an image wrongly in it emits a RUN that
671	// fails at build. A private base (`registry.example.com/base:1`) says nothing
672	// about its distribution and is therefore never accepted.
673	var debianFamilyBases = map[string]bool{
674		"debian": true, "ubuntu": true,
675		"golang": true, "node": true, "python": true, "ruby": true,
676		"rust": true, "php": true, "perl": true, "openjdk": true,
677		"maven": true, "gradle": true, "eclipse-temurin": true,
678	}
679	
680	// isDebianFamily says whether ref's adduser takes Debian's flags.
681	//
682	// An "alpine" anywhere in the reference disqualifies it whatever the repository
683	// says — `golang:1.23-alpine` is busybox — and so does a digest with no tag,
684	// where nothing names the variant.
685	func isDebianFamily(ref string) bool {
686		if ref == "" {
687			return false
688		}
689		lower := strings.ToLower(ref)
690		if strings.Contains(lower, "alpine") || strings.Contains(lower, "busybox") ||
691			strings.Contains(lower, "distroless") || strings.Contains(lower, "scratch") {
692			return false
693		}
694	
695		repo := lower
696		if i := strings.LastIndexAny(repo, ":@"); i >= 0 {
697			repo = repo[:i]
698		}
699		// Only an official image, which is a bare name with no registry or user in
700		// front of it. Anything namespaced is somebody's own build.
701		if strings.Contains(repo, "/") {
702			return false
703		}
704		return debianFamilyBases[repo]
705	}
706	
707	// lineEnding returns what this file separates its lines with, so an inserted
708	// block does not mix LF into a CRLF file.
709	func lineEnding(content []byte) string {
710		if i := indexByte(content, '\n'); i > 0 && content[i-1] == '\r' {
711			return "\r\n"
712		}
713		return "\n"
714	}
715	
716	func indexByte(b []byte, c byte) int {
717		for i := range b {
718			if b[i] == c {
719				return i
720			}
721		}
722		return -1
723	}
724	
725	// insertionPoint finds where a USER instruction has to go in the stage that
726	// starts at the 1-based line finalFrom: just before that stage's first CMD or
727	// ENTRYPOINT, or at eof when it has neither.
728	//
729	// It also answers whether the stage already sets a user, because that is the
730	// same single pass — asking twice would let the two answers disagree about
731	// where the stage ends.
732	func insertionPoint(lines []contentLine, finalFrom, eof int) (at int, alreadySet bool) {
733		for i := finalFrom; i < len(lines); i++ {
734			switch instruction(lines[i].text) {
735			case "USER":
736				return 0, true
737			case "CMD", "ENTRYPOINT":
738				return lines[i].off, false
739			}
740		}
741		return eof, false
742	}
743	
744	// instruction returns the leading keyword of a Dockerfile line, uppercased, or
745	// "" for a blank line, a comment, or a continuation of the line before it.
746	//
747	// It does not follow continuations, and does not need to: it is only ever asked
748	// whether a line *starts* an instruction, and a continued line never does.
749	func instruction(text string) string {
750		t := strings.TrimSpace(text)
751		if t == "" || strings.HasPrefix(t, "#") {
752			return ""
753		}
754		word, _, _ := strings.Cut(t, " ")
755		word, _, _ = strings.Cut(word, "\t")
756		return strings.ToUpper(word)
757	}
758	
759	// keywordSpan returns the byte span of a line's leading token — its
760	// instruction keyword, exactly as written, case included. Unlike
761	// instruction(), which uppercases for comparison, a caller replacing the
762	// keyword needs the real span to build a patch.Edit whose Old matches what
763	// Rewrite will find there.
764	func keywordSpan(l contentLine) (patch.Span, bool) {
765		start := 0
766		for start < len(l.text) && (l.text[start] == ' ' || l.text[start] == '\t') {
767			start++
768		}
769		end := start
770		for end < len(l.text) && l.text[end] != ' ' && l.text[end] != '\t' {
771			end++
772		}
773		if start == end {
774			return patch.Span{}, false
775		}
776		return patch.Span{Start: l.off + start, End: l.off + end}, true
777	}
778	
779	// stripContinuations turns a backslash immediately followed by a newline —
780	// Dockerfile's line-continuation marker — into a space, so a multi-line
781	// instruction tokenizes as the one shell command it is instead of leaving the
782	// backslash as a stray token of its own.
783	func stripContinuations(text string) string {
784		text = strings.ReplaceAll(text, "\\\r\n", " ")
785		return strings.ReplaceAll(text, "\\\n", " ")
786	}
787	
788	type contentLine struct {
789		off  int
790		text string
791	}
792	
793	// contentLines cuts content into lines, keeping each one's byte offset so an
794	// edit can be placed at the start of one.
795	func contentLines(content []byte) []contentLine {
796		var out []contentLine
797		start := 0
798		for i := 0; i <= len(content); i++ {
799			if i < len(content) && content[i] != '\n' {
800				continue
801			}
802			if i == len(content) && start == len(content) {
803				break
804			}
805			out = append(out, contentLine{off: start, text: strings.TrimSuffix(string(content[start:i]), "\r")})
806			start = i + 1
807		}
808		return out
809	}
810	
811	func endsWithNewline(content []byte) bool {
812		return len(content) > 0 && content[len(content)-1] == '\n'
813	}

815	// baseName is filepath.Base for a path Trivy reported, which always uses
816	// forward slashes whatever the host.
817	func baseName(p string) string {
818		if i := strings.LastIndexByte(p, '/'); i >= 0 {
819			return p[i+1:]
820		}
821		return p
822	}

12	// A misconfiguration is not fixed the way a vulnerability is (§3.78). Trivy
13	// reports the block it faults and a Resolution written in English — a sentence,
14	// not a replacement — so there is no general way to turn one into an edit.
15	//
16	// What there is instead is a **deliberately finite** catalog: the few rules that
17	// recur often enough to be worth writing by hand, each with the exact edit that
18	// satisfies it. A rule absent from the catalog is not a gap to be filled. It is
19	// the case the MCP server already covers, by handing a calling agent the span,
20	// the wording and the file (phase A) and re-measuring afterwards.
21	//
22	// That boundary is the point, and it is why Fix declines instead of
23	// approximating: an absence sends the user to something that works, while a
24	// doubtful edit sends them to a diff they have to second-guess.
25	
26	// Rule is one misconfiguration this application knows how to fix on its own.
27	type Rule struct {
28		// AVDID is the rule's identity as Trivy reports it in Finding.ID. It is
29		// matched loosely — see ruleKey — because Trivy spells the same rule
30		// "AVD-DS-0002" in one field and "DS002" in another.
31		AVDID string
32		// Title is what the UI calls the fix. It says what the edit does, not what
33		// the rule forbids: the user is agreeing to a change, not reading an advisory.
34		Title string
35		// Fix returns the edits that satisfy the rule on content, or nil and a
36		// reason when this instance is not one the catalog handles.
37		//
38		// It never guesses. An instance it cannot read exactly is one it declines,
39		// and the reason is shown to the user as-is (Rule 129: English).
40		Fix func(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string)
41		// Warning is a sentence the confirmation shows with the diff when the
42		// fix reverses a choice the author may have made on purpose (DEVDESK-687).
43		// Empty for a fix that has nothing to warn about.
44		Warning string
45		// Target is the file the fix edits, when it is not the one the finding
46		// points at: a slash path relative to root, the scanned directory, or a
47		// reason when there is no file to edit. Nil edits f.File.
48		//
49		// It exists for the build context (§3.81), whose finding points at the
50		// Dockerfile line that copies everything while the fix belongs in the
51		// .dockerignore beside it. It may read the disk, so it is called where the
52		// fix is computed, never where the shortcut column is.
53		Target func(root string, f scan.Finding) (rel, reason string)
54	}

56	// FileFor returns the file this rule's fix edits for f, relative to root, or
57	// the reason there is none.
58	func (r Rule) FileFor(root string, f scan.Finding) (rel, reason string) {
59		if r.Target == nil {
60			return f.File, ""
61		}
62		return r.Target(root, f)
63	}

259	// FixFor returns the catalog's rule for a finding, if it has one.
260	//
261	// It answers for misconfigurations only. A vulnerability, a secret or a licence
262	// reaching here is not an error — the tab is shared — it simply has no rule.
263	func FixFor(f scan.Finding) (Rule, bool) {
264		if scan.Categorize(f) != scan.CategoryMisconfiguration {
265			return Rule{}, false
266		}
267		r, ok := catalog[RuleKey(f.ID)]
268		return r, ok
269	}

271	// RuleKey reduces the spellings of one rule id to a single key.
272	//
273	// Trivy writes "AVD-DS-0002" in AVDID and "DS002" in ID, and which of the two
274	// reaches a Finding has changed before. Matching on either spelling costs one
275	// function; matching on one of them costs a catalog that silently stops firing
276	// the day the other is used.
277	func RuleKey(id string) string {
278		id = strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(id))
279		id = strings.TrimPrefix(id, "AVD-")
280		id = strings.ReplaceAll(id, "-", "")
281	
282		letters := strings.IndexFunc(id, func(r rune) bool { return r >= '0' && r <= '9' })
283		if letters <= 0 {
284			return id
285		}
286		prefix, digits := id[:letters], strings.TrimLeft(id[letters:], "0")
287		if digits == "" {
288			digits = "0"
289		}
290		return prefix + digits
291	}

293	// fixRootUser satisfies "specify at least 1 USER command" by creating an
294	// unprivileged account in the final stage and switching to it.
295	//
296	// **It creates the account rather than naming a uid.** A bare `USER 10001`
297	// switches to a uid that has no passwd entry: no name, no home, no shell. Much
298	// of what runs in a container asks the system who it is — anything calling
299	// getpwuid, a shell wanting $HOME, tools that write to a home directory — and
300	// all of it degrades in ways that surface later, at run time, far from this
301	// edit. `adduser` first, `USER appuser` after, is what `docker init` generates
302	// and what this now emits.
303	//
304	// **The flags are Debian's, so the base image has to be one.** The long options
305	// below belong to the Debian/Ubuntu `adduser`; busybox's, on Alpine, takes
306	// different ones (`-D`, `-H`, `-s /sbin/nologin`) and a distroless image has no
307	// shell to run either in. Guessing wrong produces a Dockerfile that fails at
308	// build, which is worse than offering nothing — so a base this cannot identify
309	// is declined, and the agent path (phase A) takes it.
310	//
311	// The block goes before the final stage's first CMD or ENTRYPOINT, which is
312	// where it has to be to apply to the process that runs — after it, it would
313	// change nothing. With neither, it goes at the end of the file.
314	//
315	// What it does not do is chown anything. A process that loses root may no longer
316	// be able to write where it used to, and no edit computed from the Dockerfile
317	// alone can know. That is a change the user reads in the diff and agrees to, and
318	// that the re-scan then confirms cleared the rule — it is not a claim that the
319	// image still works.
320	func fixRootUser(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
321		if !dockerfile.IsDockerfileName(baseName(f.File)) {
322			return nil, ReasonNotADockerfile
323		}
324		stages := dockerfile.Parse(content).Stages
325		if len(stages) == 0 {
326			return nil, ReasonNoStage
327		}
328	
329		final := stages[len(stages)-1]
330		if !isDebianFamily(final.Image) {
331			return nil, ReasonUnknownBaseFamily
332		}
333	
334		lines := contentLines(content)
335		if final.Line > len(lines) {
336			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
337		}
338	
339		at, already := insertionPoint(lines, final.Line, len(content))
340		if already {
341			return nil, ReasonAlreadyFixed
342		}
343	
344		text := addUserBlock(lineEnding(content))
345		if at == len(content) && !endsWithNewline(content) {
346			text = lineEnding(content) + text
347		}
348		return []patch.Edit{{Span: patch.Span{Start: at, End: at}, New: text}}, ""
349	}

351	// addUserBlock is the Debian/Ubuntu incantation, spelled out rather than
352	// condensed: every flag is there to make the account unusable for anything but
353	// running the process — no password, no home, no login shell.
354	func addUserBlock(eol string) string {
355		lines := []string{
356			"ARG UID=" + nonRootUID,
357			"RUN adduser \\",
358			`    --disabled-password \`,
359			`    --gecos "" \`,
360			`    --home "/nonexistent" \`,
361			`    --shell "/usr/sbin/nologin" \`,
362			"    --no-create-home \\",
363			`    --uid "${UID}" \`,
364			"    " + nonRootUser,
365			"USER " + nonRootUser,
366		}
367		return strings.Join(lines, eol) + eol
368	}

370	// recommendsFlag is what fixAptGetNoRecommends adds. Its position relative to
371	// "install" does not matter to apt-get, so the fix always puts it in the same
372	// place — right after "install" — rather than trying to match wherever a
373	// human might have put the rest of the command's own flags.
374	const recommendsFlag = "--no-install-recommends"
375	
376	// aptGetInstall matches an apt-get install invocation. It does not try to
377	// mirror the full breadth of Trivy's own check (flags between "apt-get" and
378	// "install" are rare enough to skip), because a match here only has to find
379	// what to fix, not decide what Trivy would flag — that decision was already
380	// made when the finding was reported.
381	var aptGetInstall = regexp.MustCompile(`apt-get\s+install\b`)
382	
383	// apkAdd matches an apk add invocation, on the same terms as aptGetInstall.
384	var apkAdd = regexp.MustCompile(`apk\s+add\b`)
385	
386	// assumeYesFlag recognizes apt-get's confirmation flag in any of the forms
387	// apt-get itself accepts: a short flag cluster containing 'y' (`-y`, `-qy`,
388	// `-yq`), or the long spellings. A literal `strings.Contains(s, "-y")` — good
389	// enough for the long, unique --no-install-recommends — would miss `-qy`.
390	var assumeYesFlag = regexp.MustCompile(`(^|\s)-[A-Za-z]*y[A-Za-z]*(\s|$)|--yes\b|--assume-yes\b`)
391	
392	// fixCommandFlag is fixAptGetNoRecommends, fixAptGetAssumeYes and
393	// fixApkNoCache's shared shape: find every invocation of the command the
394	// finding's line range covers, and add insertText right after it unless
395	// hasFlag already reports the flag present in that invocation's own
396	// statement.
397	//
398	// It only looks at the reported span, not the whole file: an invocation
399	// elsewhere in the Dockerfile is a different finding, and fixing it here
400	// would be an edit the diff never explained. Within the span, each invocation
401	// is checked on its own — a RUN chaining two of them with `&&` where only one
402	// already has the flag is not "already fixed" just because the flag appears
403	// somewhere in the line.
404	func fixCommandFlag(content []byte, f scan.Finding, command *regexp.Regexp, hasFlag func(string) bool, insertText, noMatchReason string) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
405		if !dockerfile.IsDockerfileName(baseName(f.File)) {
406			return nil, ReasonNotADockerfile
407		}
408		span, ok := lineSpan(content, f.Line, f.EndLine)
409		if !ok {
410			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
411		}
412		text := string(content[span.Start:span.End])
413	
414		matches := command.FindAllStringIndex(text, -1)
415		if matches == nil {
416			return nil, noMatchReason
417		}
418	
419		var edits []patch.Edit
420		for _, m := range matches {
421			stmtEnd := statementEnd(text, m[1])
422			if hasFlag(text[m[1]:stmtEnd]) {
423				continue
424			}
425			at := span.Start + m[1]
426			edits = append(edits, patch.Edit{Span: patch.Span{Start: at, End: at}, New: insertText})
427		}
428		if len(edits) == 0 {
429			return nil, ReasonAlreadyFixed
430		}
431		return edits, ""
432	}
433	
434	// fixAptGetNoRecommends satisfies "'apt-get' missing '--no-install-recommends'"
435	// (AVD-DS-0029).
436	func fixAptGetNoRecommends(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
437		return fixCommandFlag(content, f, aptGetInstall,
438			func(s string) bool { return strings.Contains(s, recommendsFlag) },
439			" "+recommendsFlag, ReasonNoAptGetInstall)
440	}

442	// fixAptGetAssumeYes satisfies "'apt-get' missing '-y'" (AVD-DS-0021).
443	func fixAptGetAssumeYes(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
444		return fixCommandFlag(content, f, aptGetInstall, assumeYesFlag.MatchString, " -y", ReasonNoAptGetInstall)
445	}

447	// fixApkNoCache satisfies "'apk add' is missing '--no-cache'" (AVD-DS-0025).
448	func fixApkNoCache(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
449		return fixCommandFlag(content, f, apkAdd,
450			func(s string) bool { return strings.Contains(s, "--no-cache") },
451			" --no-cache", ReasonNoApkAdd)
452	}

454	// yumInstall, dnfInstall, microdnfInstall and zypperInstall match the install
455	// invocation fixAppendCleanup looks for, one per package manager.
456	var (
457		yumInstall      = regexp.MustCompile(`yum\s+install\b`)
458		dnfInstall      = regexp.MustCompile(`dnf\s+install\b`)
459		microdnfInstall = regexp.MustCompile(`microdnf\s+install\b`)
460		zypperInstall   = regexp.MustCompile(`zypper\s+install\b`)
461	)

463	// fixAppendCleanup is fixYumClean, fixDnfClean, fixMicrodnfClean and
464	// fixZypperClean's shared shape: Trivy's own check for each of these only
465	// counts a cleanup command as satisfying it when it is the last thing the RUN
466	// does, so the fix appends cleanCmd at the very end of the reported span
467	// rather than placing it next to the install call — anywhere else, a
468	// re-scan would still flag it.
469	//
470	// It is idempotent against the one case worth checking without a full shell
471	// parse: the span, once trailing whitespace and a stray continuation
472	// backslash are trimmed, already ending in cleanCmd.
473	func fixAppendCleanup(content []byte, f scan.Finding, install *regexp.Regexp, cleanCmd, noMatchReason string) ([]patch.Edit, string) {
474		if !dockerfile.IsDockerfileName(baseName(f.File)) {
475			return nil, ReasonNotADockerfile
476		}
477		span, ok := lineSpan(content, f.Line, f.EndLine)
478		if !ok {
479			return nil, ReasonUnreadableSpan
480		}
481		text := string(content[span.Start:span.End])
482		if !install.MatchString(text) {
483			return nil, noMatchReason
484		}
485	
486		trimmed := strings.TrimRight(text, " \t\r\n")
487		trimmed = strings.TrimRight(strings.TrimSuffix(trimmed, "\\"), " \t")
488		if strings.HasSuffix(trimmed, cleanCmd) {
489			return nil, ReasonAlreadyFixed
490		}

634	// statementEnd finds where the shell statement starting at from ends: the next

638	// against whatever a later statement in the same RUN happens to contain.

653	// one physical line, and a finding that predates EndLine still names one.

655		if endLine < startLine {

670	// declined, which costs a fix, while an image wrongly in it emits a RUN that

673	var debianFamilyBases = map[string]bool{

726	// starts at the 1-based line finalFrom: just before that stage's first CMD or
727	// ENTRYPOINT, or at eof when it has neither.

730	// same single pass — asking twice would let the two answers disagree about
731	// where the stage ends.
732	func insertionPoint(lines []contentLine, finalFrom, eof int) (at int, alreadySet bool) {

734			switch instruction(lines[i].text) {
735			case "USER":

737			case "CMD", "ENTRYPOINT":

744	// instruction returns the leading keyword of a Dockerfile line, uppercased, or
745	// "" for a blank line, a comment, or a continuation of the line before it.
746	//

748	// whether a line *starts* an instruction, and a continued line never does.
749	func instruction(text string) string {
750		t := strings.TrimSpace(text)
751		if t == "" || strings.HasPrefix(t, "#") {
752			return ""
753		}
754		word, _, _ := strings.Cut(t, " ")
755		word, _, _ = strings.Cut(word, "\t")
756		return strings.ToUpper(word)

760	// instruction keyword, exactly as written, case included. Unlike
761	// instruction(), which uppercases for comparison, a caller replacing the
762	// keyword needs the real span to build a patch.Edit whose Old matches what
763	// Rewrite will find there.
764	func keywordSpan(l contentLine) (patch.Span, bool) {
765		start := 0
766		for start < len(l.text) && (l.text[start] == ' ' || l.text[start] == '\t') {
767			start++
768		}
769		end := start
770		for end < len(l.text) && l.text[end] != ' ' && l.text[end] != '\t' {
771			end++
772		}
773		if start == end {
774			return patch.Span{}, false
775		}
776		return patch.Span{Start: l.off + start, End: l.off + end}, true

779	// stripContinuations turns a backslash immediately followed by a newline —
780	// Dockerfile's line-continuation marker — into a space, so a multi-line
781	// instruction tokenizes as the one shell command it is instead of leaving the
782	// backslash as a stray token of its own.
783	func stripContinuations(text string) string {
784		text = strings.ReplaceAll(text, "\\\r\n", " ")
785		return strings.ReplaceAll(text, "\\\n", " ")
786	}
787	
788	type contentLine struct {
789		off  int
790		text string
791	}
792	
793	// contentLines cuts content into lines, keeping each one's byte offset so an
794	// edit can be placed at the start of one.
795	func contentLines(content []byte) []contentLine {
796		var out []contentLine
797		start := 0
798		for i := 0; i <= len(content); i++ {
799			if i < len(content) && content[i] != '\n' {
800				continue
801			}
802			if i == len(content) && start == len(content) {
803				break
804			}
805			out = append(out, contentLine{off: start, text: strings.TrimSuffix(string(content[start:i]), "\r")})
806			start = i + 1
807		}
808		return out
809	}
810	
811	func endsWithNewline(content []byte) bool {
812		return len(content) > 0 && content[len(content)-1] == '\n'
813	}

817	func baseName(p string) string {
818		if i := strings.LastIndexByte(p, '/'); i >= 0 {

820		}
821		return p

14	)

16	// Why a KSV-0104 finding fired (DEVDESK-686, S-01). Trivy words the finding the
17	// same for an explicit Unconfined and for a missing seccomp profile, and
18	// points at the container's block rather than at the line that says
19	// Unconfined, so neither the message nor the span tells the two apart. The
20	// manifest is read again at scan time, the way the Kubernetes fixes read it
21	// (§3.80): the document at the reported line, the container by its name inside
22	// the reported lines.
23	const (
24		SeccompUnconfined = "unconfined"
25		SeccompAbsent     = "absent"
26	)
27	
28	// seccompContainer is how KSV-0104 names its container: lower case and double
29	// quotes, unlike the other KSV rules ("Container 'api' of …").
30	var seccompContainer = regexp.MustCompile(`container "([^"]+)"`)
31	
32	// isSeccompRule reports whether id is KSV-0104, in any of the three spellings
33	// Trivy and the cache have used. This package cannot import remediation, where
34	// RuleKey lives.
35	func isSeccompRule(id string) bool {
36		id = strings.ReplaceAll(strings.TrimPrefix(strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(id)), "AVD-"), "-", "")
37		return id == "KSV0104" || id == "KSV104"
38	}
39	
40	// indexDocuments decodes a manifest once; a variable so a test can count the
41	// decodes.
42	var indexDocuments = k8s.IndexDocuments
43

45	func annotateSeccomp(root string, findings []Finding) {
46		annotateSeccompContext(context.Background(), root, findings)
47	}
48

50	// of a directory scan, reading and decoding each file once however many
51	// findings point into it. It never fails the scan: whatever it cannot confirm
52	// leaves the origin empty, which reads as "unknown". It stops between files
53	// once ctx is done.
54	func annotateSeccompContext(ctx context.Context, root string, findings []Finding) {
55		byFile := map[string][]int{}
56		for i, f := range findings {
57			if f.Source == SourceTrivyMisconfig && f.IaCType == "kubernetes" && isSeccompRule(f.ID) {
58				byFile[f.File] = append(byFile[f.File], i)
59			}
60		}

# TUI — Bubble Tea behavior & architecture

### Rule 109 : Bubble Tea message naming convention

- Format: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg`
- Examples: `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`, `ConfirmModalYesMsg`
- Always document with a comment
- Group related messages together in the file

### Rule 110 : NEVER modify the model inside a Cmd ⚠️

**Fundamental principle of Bubble Tea (Elm architecture).**

`Update()`, `View()`, and `Cmd`s execute in parallel. Modifying the model inside a Cmd creates race conditions detectable with `go run -race`.

| Component | Role | Can modify the model? |
|-----------|------|---------------------------|
| `Update()` | Processes messages | ✅ YES (the only allowed place) |
| `View()` | Renders the UI | ❌ NO (read-only) |
| `Cmd` | Async I/O operations | ❌ NO (returns messages) |

```go
// ❌ WRONG — race condition
func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    return func() tea.Msg {
        m.authenticated = false  // DANGER
        return nil
    }
}

// ✅ CORRECT — message + Update()
type LogoutCompleteMsg struct{}

func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    url := m.urlInput.Value()  // copy the data we need
    return func() tea.Msg {
        auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(m.storage)
        _ = auth.Logout(url)
        return LogoutCompleteMsg{}
    }
}

case LogoutCompleteMsg:
    m.authenticated = false  // thread-safe inside Update()
    m.user = nil
    return m, nil
```

**Golden rule**: Cmds do the "dirty work" (I/O), then send a message to `Update()`.

### Rule 126 : Scan cache behavior (Images & Workspaces)

| Action | Disk cache | Memory cache | Scan triggered |
|--------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| `Enter` (scanned item) | Read | Read | No |
| `Enter` (not scanned) | — | — | No |
| `ctrl+s` (in progress) | Blocked | Blocked | No |
| `ctrl+s` (available) | Overwritten | Updated | Yes (item only) |
| `A` (unscanned) | Unchanged | Unchanged | Yes (unscanned) |
| `ctrl+a` (all) | **Purged** | **Purged** | Yes (all) |

**`ctrl+a` must clear the cache before relaunching the scans:**
```go
// ✅ CORRECT
func (m Model) requestScanAll() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    var keys []string
    for _, img := range m.images {
        delete(m.scanCache, name)  // in-memory purge inside Update()
        keys = append(keys, name)
    }
    return m, tea.Batch(deleteScanCacheCmd(keys), batchScanCmd(keys, m.defaultScanOpts()))
}
```

### Rule 128 : Footer messages — three levels, centered, one component

**`components.FooterMessage` is the only implementation.** A view does not
render its own message: it declares one, sets it from `Update()`, and
renders it via `m.footer.View(width, status)`.

There used to be eight of them, one per view, each with its own fields,
timer, and lipgloss block. That is what produced the flaw this component
removes: nobody ever centered the error branch, in any of the eight, so
errors were left-aligned everywhere while notices were centered.

#### The three levels

They are defined by **what happened**, not by how it feels:

| Level | Meaning | Color |
|--------|------|---------|
| `Error` | an operation failed, or the system refused it | `ColorFooterError` = the red of **CRITICAL** CVEs |
| `Warn` | the action cannot be honored as requested, but nothing failed: an unmet precondition, already in progress, not applicable here | `ColorFooterWarn` = the orange of **MEDIUM** CVEs |
| `Info` | a neutral fact, or a successful operation | `ColorFooterInfo` = `ColorText`, the ordinary text color |

Info is not bold, the other two are: the hierarchy runs through weight as
much as through hue, and a neutral info in bold would turn back into an
alert.

The colors are **semantic aliases** assigned in `ApplyTheme` (`colors.go`),
like the viewer's syntax colors: no theme file gains a key. They target the
**severity** names rather than `ColorError` / `ColorWarn` — the default
theme makes them coincide, so the choice is invisible today; it stops being
invisible in a theme that separates them.

#### What is forbidden

- ❌ `theme.StatusErrorStyle`, `StatusOKStyle`, `StatusWarningStyle`, or
  `ColorHighlight` inside a `RenderFooter`, a `renderInfoLine`, or a
  `renderInfoText` — `TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage` scans the sources
  and fails, naming the file, line, and function.
- ❌ **Green** in a footer. It is reserved for status icons (Rule 121).
- ❌ A **left-aligned** message. `View` centers, always, across the full
  width.
- ❌ A local timer (`clearFooterCmd`, `clearInfoMsgCmd`, …): the component
  carries it.

#### Mandatory pattern

```go
// 1. The model declares a field.
type Model struct {
    footer sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
}

// 2. Update() sets the message and returns its timer. A message set without
//    its timer never disappears.
case SomeErrorMsg:
    log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", msg.Err)
    return m, m.footer.Error("Failed to load data — check logs")

case ScanAlreadyRunningMsg:
    return m, m.footer.Warn("Scan already in progress")

// 3. Update() offers unhandled messages to the component, which consumes
//    the expiry addressed to it.
m.footer.Handle(msg)
return m, nil

// 4. RenderFooter() renders the line, blank included — Rule 124 budgets it.
func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(width) + "
" + m.footer.View(width, m.status())
}
```

**The expiry carries an id** (`ClearFooterMsg{ID}`): a stale timer does not
clear the message that took its predecessor's place. That is what makes the
type shareable across packages, and it fixes, in passing, a flaw all eight
implementations shared — a message set at t+2.9s was cleared at t+3s by the
previous one's timer.

#### `Status` — what has no timer

A progress indicator, a hint, a loading state: these are **states**, not
events. They are derived on every frame and passed as `View`'s second
argument, never set as a message — a line set when the first repo starts
would be cleared while the tenth is still running.

```go
func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
    if m.loading && len(m.table.Items()) == 0 {
        // the view's own load: the shared dot, with WantsBlink
        return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: "Loading images...", Activity: true}
    }
    // work the router tracks (a run in the registry): the shared dot
    return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.progressLine(), Activity: m.anyRunning()}
}
```

Precedence in `View`: **error → warning → info → status**. A failure the
user has not read takes priority over the progress of whatever is still
running.

One field prefixes the line with a mark:

| Field | Mark | Use it for | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Activity: true` | the shared activity dot, `●` / `○` (same glyph and colour as the row dots, `indicator.Running`) | any loading or running state: work the **router tracks** (a run in the jobs registry) and a view's own load (`WantsBlink()`) | the router's 500 ms blink phase: the view calls `m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` from its `jobs.FrameMsg` handler |

The braille spinner is removed (DEVDESK-377): `Status.Spinner`,
`FooterMessage.SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` and
`theme.SpinnerStyle` no longer exist, and no file under `internal/` may import
`charm.land/bubbles/v2/spinner`. `TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner` and
`TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone` (`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`)
fail on a reintroduction, with no exception. `dk setup` has no router: it shows
a fixed `●` and the pending text, with no blink. Without a `SetBlinkPhase`
call the dot is steady on. `●` and `○` are one column wide and share a width,
so the phase never shifts the text.

A future `Activity` value that does not depend on the jobs registry must make
its view implement `WantsBlink() bool` (return `status().Activity`, as the
forge explorer does); otherwise the router arms no animation chain and the dot
stays fixed on `●`.

#### A table's loading state belongs to the footer

**When a `datatable` is loading, the table stays on screen** and the
loading state is an info message with a mark (the shared activity dot, for the
view's own load as well as for work the router tracks), in the footer only. A body that replaces itself with a loading screen loses its header and columns for the
duration of every `ctrl+r`, then regains them: a layout jump on every
refresh.

**A footer mark is for a table's data loading, never for one row.**
What is happening to a single row (a scan, a clone, a stop) is that row's
activity dot (Rule 125, "The activity column"); when the selected row has a
footer detail with a glyph (`Detail.Glyph`), the footer shows no dot: the
row's own dot already moves.

Mandatory consequence: the empty message ("No images found") is
**conditioned on loading being finished**, otherwise the table announces the
absence of what it is still looking for.

`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` (`internal/ui/components`) rejects a
loading body in the table views it covers. There is no declared exception.

#### Tests — the timer really does sleep

`tea.Tick` blocks for its entire duration, and `testutil.Msgs` runs the
whole batch it is given: a test that inspects a `Cmd` carrying the timer
pays the full three seconds. The timer starts when the `Cmd` is **built**
(`PostFooter` and `FooterMessage.set` call `tea.Tick` at that moment), not
when it runs: shortening the duration after the `Update` that returned the
`Cmd` is too late, the three seconds are already armed.

- To verify that a message **disappears**, build the expiry rather than
  running the `Cmd`:
  `feed(t, m, components.ClearFooterMsg{ID: m.footer.ID()})`.
- For a test that must drain the `Cmd` (because it is looking for another
  one inside it), shorten the timer **before the `Update` that builds the
  `Cmd`**, as the first line of the test:
  `testutil.FastTimers(t, &components.FooterMsgDuration)`. A helper that
  drains a `Cmd` (like `drive` in `internal/app`) only covers the `Cmds` it
  builds itself.
- `requireNoRealFooterWait(t)` (`internal/app/footer_timer_guard_test.go`)
  fails a test that took over 1.5 s: use it in a test that builds and drains
  footer `Cmds`.

`FooterMsgDuration` is an exported `var` for this reason alone; its
production value is fixed by `TestAMessageGetsThreeSeconds`.

#### Other prohibitions

Mandatory log format: `log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", err)`

- ❌ `err.Error()` directly in the UI (except a validation message already
  written to be read)
- ❌ Replacing the view with an error screen (except fatal initialization
  errors)
- ❌ Ignoring an error without `log.Printf`

# TUI — Forms & Focus

### Rule 103 : Standardized form navigation

- `↑ / ↓` to navigate between a form's fields
- A visual indicator (`theme.IconCircleSmall`) must show the focused element
- `Enter` to validate action buttons only (see Rule 135)

### Rule 104 : Modal window structure

- Rounded border (NormalBorder) with color appropriate to the context
- Title at the top using `theme.TitleStyle`
- Message in the center
- Buttons at the bottom with consistent spacing
- Help instructions with `theme.HelpStyle` at the very bottom
- Safe choice by default (e.g. "No" for delete confirmations)

**Palette variant (selector, Rule 112).** Border and title only: the title sits in
the top border, the border is `theme.ColorPaletteBorder`, there are no buttons and
no help line (Rule 134; the header lists the keys). Every line has an explicit
background and the exact width of the frame.

### Rule 113 : Form field spacing

| Layout | Separator after the field |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Multi-line**: label ↵ content | `\n\n` (blank line) |
| **Single-line**: label + content on the same line | `\n` |
| **Checkboxes** | `\n` between them, `\n\n` after the group |

`renderField()` functions must **NOT** include the trailing separator.

### Rule 114 : Built-in help system (`?`)

**Every view implements `help.Provider` via `GetHelpContent()`, always in English.**

Obligations:
- Mandatory update in the same commit whenever a feature / keybinding changes
- Every new view must implement `help.Provider` with complete content

Expected content: `Title`, `Description`, `KeyBindings`, `Sections`

Files:
- `internal/ui/help/help.go` — component and `Provider` interface
- `internal/ui/*/view.go` or `model.go` — per-view implementation

**Declared gap: the command palette has no in-app help.** It is not a view; its
keys (`↑↓`, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`) are in the header while it is open and
documented in `docs-site/docs/reference/commands.md` (DEVDESK-89, decision of
the user).

### Rule 120 : Focus indicator and form field rendering

**Indentation: 2 characters.** When focused, `theme.IconCircleSmall` sits at column 0.

| State | Prefix |
|------|---------|
| Focused | `IconCircleSmall + " "` → `● Label` |
| Not focused | `"  "` (2 spaces) → `  Label` |

`theme.IconCircleSmall` (`\ueb8a`) does NOT contain a space — always add `" "` after it.

**Label/value separator**: `theme.IconChevronRight` (`\uf054`) + `" "`. **No `:`**.

**A space before the chevron is mandatory**: there must always be a space between the label text and `IconChevronRight`.

```go
// ✅ Single-line, focused
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()

// ✅ Multi-ligne
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name " + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()

// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
```

**Selection lists**: `IconCircleSmall` for the selected item, `"  "` for the others.

**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.

**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).

**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.

**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.

Forbidden:
- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for focused elements (use `ColorHighlight`)
- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form

### Rule 131 : Top padding for forms in the viewport

**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +
        f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — two blank lines (EmptyLineBg + "\n\n")
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return f.renderFields()
}
```

Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).

### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)

**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**

It is the **only** control allowed for a closed set. Radio buttons are not
an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
a different thing from an exclusive choice.

#### Visual

```
  Visibility  󰅂 private        ← not focused
● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)
```

Line structure:

| Part | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |

#### Navigation

- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)
- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: navigate to the previous / next field

Do not use `Enter` to cycle — `Enter` confirms the form or advances to the next field.

#### Reference implementation

```go
// Rendu
func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
    }
    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

// Key handling
case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
    }
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)

### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses

Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:

| State | Icon |
|------|-------|
| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |

Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).

**Amendment (DEVDESK-137): the activity column is not covered.** In the activity
column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed
`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases, and not `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning`.
Every other status column (Verdict, Update, Sig, scan results, UP/DOWN) keeps
the three icons above, unchanged.

### Rule 133 : Multi-line text fields — `WrappedInput` mandatory

**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).

Use **`components.WrappedInput`** (`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go`) for any text field that must display across multiple lines.

#### API

```go
// Creation
field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")

// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)

// Focus / Blur
field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()

// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
field, cmd = field.Update(msg)

// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()

// Retrieving the value on submit
value := field.Value()
```

#### `wrapWidth` parameter

`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).

| Context | Recommended value |
|----------|--------------------|
| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
| Short notes field | `60` |
| Long text field | `100` |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
const descWrapWidth = 80
descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")

// ❌ WRONG
descInput := textarea.New()
```

#### Behavior

- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`

### Rule 103 : Standardized form navigation

- `↑ / ↓` to navigate between a form's fields
- A visual indicator (`theme.IconCircleSmall`) must show the focused element
- `Enter` to validate action buttons only (see Rule 135)

### Rule 104 : Modal window structure

- Rounded border (NormalBorder) with color appropriate to the context
- Title at the top using `theme.TitleStyle`
- Message in the center
- Buttons at the bottom with consistent spacing
- Help instructions with `theme.HelpStyle` at the very bottom
- Safe choice by default (e.g. "No" for delete confirmations)

**Palette variant (selector, Rule 112).** Border and title only: the title sits in
the top border, the border is `theme.ColorPaletteBorder`, there are no buttons and
no help line (Rule 134; the header lists the keys). Every line has an explicit
background and the exact width of the frame.

### Rule 113 : Form field spacing

| Layout | Separator after the field |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Multi-line**: label ↵ content | `\n\n` (blank line) |
| **Single-line**: label + content on the same line | `\n` |
| **Checkboxes** | `\n` between them, `\n\n` after the group |

`renderField()` functions must **NOT** include the trailing separator.

### Rule 114 : Built-in help system (`?`)

**Every view implements `help.Provider` via `GetHelpContent()`, always in English.**

Obligations:
- Mandatory update in the same commit whenever a feature / keybinding changes
- Every new view must implement `help.Provider` with complete content

Expected content: `Title`, `Description`, `KeyBindings`, `Sections`

Files:
- `internal/ui/help/help.go` — component and `Provider` interface
- `internal/ui/*/view.go` or `model.go` — per-view implementation

**Declared gap: the command palette has no in-app help.** It is not a view; its
keys (`↑↓`, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`) are in the header while it is open and
documented in `docs-site/docs/reference/commands.md` (DEVDESK-89, decision of
the user).

### Rule 120 : Focus indicator and form field rendering

**Indentation: 2 characters.** When focused, `theme.IconCircleSmall` sits at column 0.

| State | Prefix |
|------|---------|
| Focused | `IconCircleSmall + " "` → `● Label` |
| Not focused | `"  "` (2 spaces) → `  Label` |

`theme.IconCircleSmall` (`\ueb8a`) does NOT contain a space — always add `" "` after it.

**Label/value separator**: `theme.IconChevronRight` (`\uf054`) + `" "`. **No `:`**.

**A space before the chevron is mandatory**: there must always be a space between the label text and `IconChevronRight`.

```go
// ✅ Single-line, focused
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()

// ✅ Multi-ligne

theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()

// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
```

**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.

**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).

**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.

**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.

- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)

- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form

**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +

}

func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return f.renderFields()
}
```

Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).

### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)

**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**

an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
a different thing from an exclusive choice.

#### Visual

```

● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)

Line structure:

| Part | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |

- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)

```go
// Rendu
func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
    }
    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

// Key handling
case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
    }
```

- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)

// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate

// Retrieving the value on submit

```

|----------|--------------------|
| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
| Short notes field | `60` |
| Long text field | `100` |

```

theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()

theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name " + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()

// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
```

**Selection lists**: `IconCircleSmall` for the selected item, `"  "` for the others.

**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.

**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).

**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.

**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.

Forbidden:
- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for focused elements (use `ColorHighlight`)
- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form

### Rule 131 : Top padding for forms in the viewport

**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +
        f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — two blank lines (EmptyLineBg + "\n\n")
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return f.renderFields()
}
```

Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).

### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)

**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**

It is the **only** control allowed for a closed set. Radio buttons are not
an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
a different thing from an exclusive choice.

#### Visual

```
  Visibility  󰅂 private        ← not focused
● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)
```

Line structure:

| Part | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |

#### Navigation

- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)
- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: navigate to the previous / next field

Do not use `Enter` to cycle — `Enter` confirms the form or advances to the next field.

#### Reference implementation

```go
// Rendu
func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
    }
    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

// Key handling
case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
    }
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)

### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses

Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:

| State | Icon |
|------|-------|
| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |

Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).

**Amendment (DEVDESK-137): the activity column is not covered.** In the activity
column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed
`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases, and not `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning`.
Every other status column (Verdict, Update, Sig, scan results, UP/DOWN) keeps
the three icons above, unchanged.

### Rule 133 : Multi-line text fields — `WrappedInput` mandatory

**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).

Use **`components.WrappedInput`** (`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go`) for any text field that must display across multiple lines.

#### API

```go
// Creation
field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")

// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)

// Focus / Blur
field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()

// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
field, cmd = field.Update(msg)

// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()

// Retrieving the value on submit
value := field.Value()
```

#### `wrapWidth` parameter

`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).

| Context | Recommended value |
|----------|--------------------|
| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
| Short notes field | `60` |
| Long text field | `100` |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
const descWrapWidth = 80
descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")

// ❌ WRONG
descInput := textarea.New()
```

#### Behavior

- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`
- Filled field → word-wrapped text, each line padded with `theme.PadWithBg` up to `displayWidth`
- Inverted block cursor (`ColorText` bg / `ColorBackground` fg) at the exact caret position

Forbidden:
- ❌ `bubbles/textarea` in any view
- ❌ Recreating the word-wrap or cursor logic locally
- ❌ Forgetting to call `SetDisplayWidth` in the `tea.WindowSizeMsg` handler

### Rule 135 : Strict keybinding assignment in forms ⚠️

**Every key has a single, unambiguous role.** These rules apply to every form in the application without exception.

| Key | Exclusive role |
|--------|---------------|
| `↑ / ↓` | Navigate between a form's fields |
| `Tab / Shift+Tab` | Switch between tabs **only** — never for navigation between fields |
| `Space` | Toggle a checkbox — the **only** key allowed for this role |
| `Enter` | Validate an action button or trigger a specific action — **never** to toggle a checkbox |
| `← / →` | Change level in a table (drill-down/up) **and** cycle the values of a closed-list field |
| `Esc` | Cancel / close / return to the parent level |

**Declared exception: the command line.** `tab` completes the highlighted
suggestion there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`). The
command line has no tabs and no fields, so neither job of `tab` exists on it.

**Declared exception: the `g` prompt.** `tab` switches the search mode between
fuzzy and exact there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `fuzzy/finder`,
DEVDESK-678). The prompt has no tabs and no fields to walk through, so neither
job of `tab` exists on it. The key is listed in the shortcuts header, named after
the mode it switches to.

#### Detailed rules

**`Tab / Shift+Tab` — tabs only**
- Reserved for switching between tabs (`bubbles/table` breadcrumb, result tabs, etc.)
- Must **never** be used to move forward/backward between form fields
- If a view has no tabs, `Tab` must do nothing (or be ignored)

**`↑ / ↓` — navigation between fields**
- The only keys to move focus from one field to another in a form
- In a list/table outside a form: row-by-row movement (Rule 111)

**`Space` — toggle checkbox**
- The only valid key to check/uncheck a checkbox
- Match it as `keymap.Space`, never as a `" "` literal (Bubble Tea v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`; `keymap.Space` is `"space"`); `TestNoKeyIsComparedToALiteralSpace` fails on a literal
- Reference implementation: `LaunchForm` (`internal/ui/oci_resources`), pinned by `launch_form_keys_test.go` — `TestLaunchFormSpaceTogglesEachCheckbox`, `TestLaunchFormDetachAndInteractiveExcludeEachOther`, `TestLaunchFormEnterNeverTogglesACheckbox`
- `Enter` on a checkbox must be ignored or advance to the next field, never toggle it
- **Confirmation buttons are the mirror case**: `Space` never answers Yes or No. `components.ConfirmModal`, `ChoiceModal`, `OptionConfirmModal` and the setup wizard's confirmation answer on `enter` only (plus `y`/`n` on the yes/no ones). In `OptionConfirmModal`, `space` toggles the option checkbox when it has focus (inert when locked) and `enter` on that checkbox is ignored

**`Enter` — validation / action**
- Validates the currently focused button
- Triggers a contextual action (e.g. launch a scan, open a detail view)
- Must **not** toggle a checkbox

**`← / →` — table navigation and value cycling**
- In a table: `←` moves up a level (drill up), `→` moves down a level (drill down)
- On a closed-list field (cycle field): `←` previous value, `→` next value (Rule 132)
- Must **not** move focus between form fields

#### Common violations to avoid

```go
// ❌ WRONG — Tab to navigate between fields
case "tab":
    m.focusedField = (m.focusedField + 1) % fieldCount

// ❌ WRONG — Enter to toggle a checkbox
case "enter":
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — Space to toggle
case keymap.Space:
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — ↑/↓ to navigate between fields
case "up":
    m.focusedField = max(m.focusedField-1, 0)
case "down":
    m.focusedField = min(m.focusedField+1, fieldCount-1)
```

### Rule 140 : An invalid field is underlined, and the footer says why (DEVDESK-292)

**A field that fails validation gets a wavy red underline, and the same error is in the footer. The underline is never the only carrier.**

- **One entry point.** The underline comes from `theme.StyleInvalidField(base)` (curly underline, `UnderlineCurly`, colour `theme.ColorInvalidField`). Never call `Underline*` anywhere else: `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint` fails the suite. For a `textinput` use `theme.SetTextInputInvalid(&ti, invalid)`; for a `WrappedInput`, `SetInvalid(bool)`.
- **Colour.** `theme.ColorInvalidField` is a closed alias of `ColorFooterError` (no theme key, Rule 119). Its contrast against `ColorBackground` is at least 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11), tested on every shipped theme.
- **The message is in the footer, level Error (Rule 128)**, taken from `components.Validation.Status()`. It is derived on every render, so it does not vanish after 3 s like a timed `footer.Error()`. The parent view returns it from its status function while the form is open.
- **Nothing is invalid before the first refused submit.** After it, every change revalidates the whole form (`Validation.Revalidate`) and the footer follows.
- **A required field left empty:** its placeholder is underlined. A focused empty `WrappedInput` shows a cursor, not its placeholder: nothing to underline, the footer carries the message.
- **Spaces are not underlined** (`UnderlineSpaces(false)`), otherwise the `textinput` padding would be underlined across the whole width. A value made only of spaces is therefore not underlined: the footer is the only carrier.
- **Restyle on a change of state only.** `SetTextInputInvalid` resets the cursor blink (`IsBlinked` goes back to false), so calling it on every message freezes the cursor. Go through `components.InvalidMarks.Sync(key, &ti, invalid)`, from `Update()` only (Rule 110), never from `View()` or a `Cmd`.
- **Prefix unchanged.** The focus prefix `●` stays as in Rule 120. The underline adds no cell: the rendered width does not change.
- **Fallback.** A terminal without styled underlines gets a plain underline (SGR 4), still readable. Cost: about 60 bytes per underlined character. Risk: SGR 58 and `4:3` on old terminals, to check by hand.

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — state change only, in Update()
f.validation.Revalidate(f.errors())
f.marks.Sync(keyName, &f.nameInput, f.validation.Invalid(keyName))

// ❌ WRONG — a local underline, and a restyle on every message
f.nameInput.SetStyles(lipgloss.NewStyle().Underline(true)...)
theme.SetTextInputInvalid(&f.nameInput, true) // in every Update
```

Forms covered, and where the rules live: `docs/architecture/ui-components.md` ("Invalid form fields"). Netdiag is covered for the Diagnostics form's Target field when the Trace Path button is pressed (DEVDESK-470). Out of scope: `templates/form.go`, the rest of netdiag (Port, DNS Server), the `ctrl+p` palette, `FilterBar`.

Guards: `internal/ui/theme/source_guard_test.go` (`TestGuardNoHexColorOutsideColorsGo`, `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint`, `TestGuardDetectors`).

</system-reminder>
